# parity-fuzz --mode subscript baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode subscript --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean (four seeds).
#
# Covers array/assoc subscripting: plain and negative indices, slices, and the
# search flags from c:Src/params.c:1367 getarg — `r R k K i I w f e n b p s`.
#
# The mode already existed and ran clean, but was NOT gated in CI, so nothing
# stopped a regression in it. Gating is what makes that clean run mean
# something. `trap` and `redir` sat in exactly this state and each turned out
# to be hiding real bugs once their vocabulary was widened — a clean ungated
# mode is an untested mode, not a correct one.
#
# The vocabulary only generated `r R i I e n b`. Adding `K w f p s` and, more
# importantly, widening the `b` indices is what found the bug below.
#
# The divergence this mode found was a real port bug and is FIXED:
#
#   The `(b:N:)` begin-index was CLAMPED rather than bounds-checked
#   (c:Src/params.c:1741-1748):
#
#       len = arrlen(ta);
#       if (beg < 0) beg += len;
#       if (down) {                    /* reverse: (I)/(R) */
#           if (beg < 0) return 0;
#       } else if (beg >= len)         /* forward: (i)/(r) */
#           return len + 1;
#       if (beg >= 0 && beg < len) {   /* the search runs ONLY in range */
#           if (down) { if (!hasbeg) beg = len - 1; ...
#
#   zshrs clamped an out-of-range begin to the nearest valid element and
#   searched from there, and floored a negative one to 0 instead of counting it
#   back from the end:
#
#       dup=(x y x y x)
#       ${dup[(Ib:6:)x]}    zsh 0    was 5
#       ${dup[(Rb:6:)x]}    zsh ''   was x
#       ${dup[(ib:-2:)x]}   zsh 5    was 1
#       ${dup[(Ib:-2:)x]}   zsh 3    was 1
#
#   "Found nothing" has TWO answers depending on WHY, which is the part a
#   reimplementation gets wrong: forward-past-the-end is len+1 (c:1746), while
#   reverse-past-the-end — and EITHER direction still-negative after
#   `beg += len` — is 0. In-range begins cannot separate those, which is why
#   the b-indices generated here deliberately run past the end AND negative
#   (-7..=7 against a 5-element array). Restricting them to 1..=5 makes the
#   whole class pass.
#
#   Structural note, since it is what made this hard to find: FOUR
#   implementations of this search exist. The faithful one (params.rs getarg,
#   carrying the c:1748 guard) is reachable only for ASSOC subscripts;
#   fusevm_bridge.rs serves LHS writes and does not parse `b` at all; subst.rs
#   has a scalar character-index search; and the live ARRAY read path is a
#   fourth, also in subst.rs, which is where the fix landed. Adding the guard to
#   getarg changed nothing observable — verified by probing, not assumed — and
#   that is what identified the live path. Same
#   faithful-port-shadowed-by-a-reimplementation shape as substnamedir /
#   typeset_single / parse_string / dotrapargs.
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
